The smallest such constant is k = 1. I am recalling this from the known solution to this competition problem (by Feng and Golberg) and have not re-derived it here.

I did check one case. In a unit square with A₁, B₁, C₁, D₁ at the side midpoints, each corner triangle has area 1/8. So S = 1/4 and S₁ = 1/2, which only forces k ≥ 1/2. The extremal configurations that push the required k up to 1 are degenerate and I did not construct them.

ANSWER: 1
